items.heading: If Your Actual Question If
items.text: If Your Actual Question If your actual question is narrow and immediate, a counselling-style session is the right, sufficient tool, don't pay for planning-level structure you don't need yet.

items.heading: The Gap Shows Up
items.text: The gap shows up in a specific way: a counselling session closes with a decision, and a decision on its own does not tell you what happens in year two or year three. Someone counselled into the "right" stream or the "right" first skill can still drift for years afterward with no milestones to check progress against and no sequence for what comes after that first choice.

items.heading: A Real Career Plan Needs
items.text: A Real Career Plan Needs A Real Career Plan Needs A real career plan needs more than one resolved decision: milestones you can check yourself against, and a skill portfolio sequenced across time, not just a direction to feel good about today.

items.heading: Paid Support, Whichever Label IT
items.text: Paid support, whichever label it carries, earns its cost once the decision or the plan gets expensive, time-pressured, or hard to reverse alone.

items.heading: No Ethical Provider Can Guarantee
items.text: No ethical provider can guarantee a specific outcome from either a counselling session or a career plan, treat a guarantee as a warning sign, not a selling point.
